name: Learn basic music notation
blurb: Enough to read a simple melody line: the staff, note values, key signatures and time signatures. It makes every other musical skill on this list cheaper to learn.
gear: Manuscript paper or a notation app
steps: Learn the treble staff, then the bass staff, using the classic mnemonics, and then practise until you no longer need them.
Learn note values and rests: whole, half, quarter, eighth, and dots and ties.
Learn time signatures and how to count each bar out loud.
Learn key signatures and the circle of fifths well enough to name the key of a piece at a glance.
Learn the common expression marks: dynamics, articulation, repeats and codas.
Sight-read one very simple new piece every day for two weeks.
tips: Rhythm is where most beginners struggle, not pitch. Clap the rhythm before you play anything.
Read music you can already play by ear first — you get instant feedback on whether you read it right.
proof: You sight-read a simple unfamiliar melody at tempo, correct notes and correct rhythm.
